info.name: matchmaking
info.description:
Complete matchmaking backend API — auth-service + matchmaking-api.

## Services
- **auth-service** (:8081) — session JWT issuance + JWKS
- **matchmaking-api** (:8080) — HTTP/WebSocket gateway (tickets, history, WS push)

## Start (order matters)
```bash
mvn -B install -DskipTests   # build + install every module FIRST
mvn -pl services/auth-service exec:java -Dexec.mainClass=com.victor.matchmaking.auth.AuthServiceApplication
mvn -pl services/matchmaking-api exec:java -Dexec.mainClass=com.victor.matchmaking.api.MatchmakingApiApplication
mvn -pl services/matchmaking-engine exec:java -Dexec.mainClass=com.victor.matchmaking.engine.MatchmakingEngineApplication
```

## Auth
Every matchmaking-api request except `/health` needs a Bearer token from `POST /v1/auth/login`.

## WebSocket
Open `WS Connect`, then send frames: PING, MATCH_CONFIRM, MATCH_DECLINE. Incoming: PONG, MATCH_PENDING_CONFIRMATION, MATCH_CONFIRMED, MATCH_CANCELLED, ERROR.

item.name: POST /v1/auth/login
item.description:
Issue a session token. In dev, login auto-provisions the player.

**Expected:** 200 with `{ "token": "...", "expiresIn": 3600 }`.
**Error:** missing/blank playerId → 400.

item.name: GET /.well-known/jwks.json
item.description:
Public keys for offline JWT validation. matchmaking-api fetches this on startup.

**Expected:** 200 with `{ "keys": [ { "kty": "RSA", "alg": "RS256", "kid": ... } ] }`.

item.name: GET /health/ready

exec: pm.test('status 200 when the dependencies answer', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.description:
Readiness probe (no auth, W18, ADR 0024).

**Expected (every dependency up):** 200 with `{"status":"UP","checks":{"redis":"UP","postgres":"UP"}}`.

**Expected (a dependency down):** 503 with the offending dependency named, e.g. `{"status":"DOWN","checks":{"redis":"DOWN","postgres":"UP"}}`. Each check is capped at 1 s, so a hung dependency answers the probe instead of holding it.

This is the endpoint a router or an orchestrator should use: `/health` stays 200 while a dependency is down (the process is fine; killing it does not fix Redis), so routing on liveness during a Redis outage sends traffic to instances that cannot serve it. `requests/resilience/verify_degradation.sh` asserts both answers with the dependency actually stopped.

item.name: POST /v1/matchmaking/tickets — rate limited (429)
item.description:
Send this request more than RATE_LIMIT_BURST times in a row (default 20) with the same player's token inside a few seconds. The token bucket lives in Redis (ratelimit:tickets:{playerId}), so the limit is per player and survives an API restart.

Expect the first RATE_LIMIT_BURST requests to answer 201 and the next ones 429 with:
- Retry-After: seconds until the next token (RATE_LIMIT_REFILL_PER_SECOND, default 5/s)
- X-RateLimit-Limit: the burst, so a client can size itself without guessing
- X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
- body: {"error": "rate limit exceeded: at most N enqueue requests are admitted per burst"}

By hand it is quicker with curl (a loop of 60 requests): this is what step 1 of requests/backpressure/verify_load_shedding.sh does, and it asserts the count stays within burst + refill × elapsed. The API counts the refusals as matchmaking_tickets_rejected_total{reason="rate_limited"} on :9090/metrics.

item.name: POST /v1/matchmaking/tickets — queue full (503)
item.description:
A queue that is deep enough to promise nobody a game admits nobody more (ADR 0022).

Precondition: the target queue holds QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH tickets (default 1000). Reach it by stopping the engine so nothing drains and enqueueing past the cap — requests/backpressure/verify_load_shedding.sh does exactly that in its step 3 (engine stopped, 1100 arrivals, 1000 admitted).

Expect 503 with Retry-After: 5 and a body naming the queue it refused for:
{"error":"queue full","queue":"queue:1v1:NA","depth":1000,"capacity":1000,"retryAfterSeconds":5}

The refusal is temporary: once the queue drains below the cap, the same request is admitted. A replay of a ticket that was already accepted is still answered while the queue is full — the player did enqueue, and refusing the retry would lose a ticket that exists. Counted as matchmaking_tickets_rejected_total{reason="queue_full"}.

item.name: POST /v1/matchmaking/tickets — hot state unavailable (503)

exec: pm.test('status 503 while Redis is down', () => pm.response.to.have.status(503));
pm.test('Retry-After tells the client when to come back', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Retry-After')).to.eql('1'));
pm.test('the body carries no internal address', () => {

item.description:
What an arrival hears when the hot state is gone (W18, ADR 0024).

Precondition: `docker stop game-matchmaking-backend-redis-1`. Start it again afterwards (`docker start game-matchmaking-backend-redis-1`) — the services do not need restarting, which is the other half of the change: their Lua SHAs reload on the next call.

Expected: **503** with `Retry-After: 1` and a body that names what is unavailable without saying where it lives:
{"error":"hot state unavailable","dependency":"redis","retryAfterSeconds":1}

Before this, the same request answered `500 {"error":"Connection refused: localhost/127.0.0.1:6379"}` — the wrong status (it tells the client to stop), plus a map of the internal network. The refusal is counted as `matchmaking_dependency_errors_total{dependency="redis"}` on the API's scrape (:9090).

Redis RESTARTED (not down) is the same endpoint answering 201: the cached script SHA is rebuilt on the first `EVALSHA` that reports `NOSCRIPT`, so a cache restart is not an outage.

item.name: GET /v1/parties/{partyId}
item.description:
Fetch a party with its aggregated skill and dispersion.

item.description:
Create a party owned by the authenticated leader.

**Expected:** 201 with `{ "partyId" }` — the party id is stored in the `partyId` environment variable.

item.description:
Add the authenticated player to a party.

**Expected:** 200 with the updated party.
**Errors:** party not found → 404; not a member → 403; party dissolved → 409.

item.description:
Remove a member. Only the party leader may remove another member.

**Expected:** 200 with the updated party, or 403 for a non-leader.

item.name: DELETE /v1/parties/{partyId}
item.description:
Dissolve a party. Only the party leader may dissolve it.

**Expected:** 200 with the dissolved party, or 403 for a non-leader.
**Errors:** unknown party → 404.

item.name: WS Connect

request.description:
Push notifications channel. Open the connection, then send frames.

**Client→server:**
- `{"type":"PING","payload":{}}` → expect `PONG`; while a match is pending, the heartbeat also **re-presents** `MATCH_PENDING_CONFIRMATION` (W19, ADR 0026: a reconnect on any instance recovers what a lost notification owed)
- `{"type":"MATCH_CONFIRM","payload":{"matchId":"..."}}` → confirm
- `{"type":"MATCH_DECLINE","payload":{"matchId":"..."}}` → decline

**Server→client:** `PONG`, `MATCH_PENDING_CONFIRMATION`, `MATCH_CONFIRMED`, `MATCH_CANCELLED`, `ERROR`.

The socket is not pinned: `presence:<playerId>` in Redis names the instance holding it (TTL 90 s), `GET /health` returns the instance's name, and any instance accepts `MATCH_CONFIRM`.

The matchmaking-engine must be running for pairing/confirmation.

Push notifications channel. Open the connection, then send frames.

item.name: routing-w19 (two instances)
item.description:
W19 (ADR 0026): the WebSocket connection is not pinned to one instance.

Start a second API instance first:
`PORT=8093 METRICS_PORT=9193 INSTANCE_ID=api-b mvn -o -q -pl services/matchmaking-api exec:java`
(the first instance stays on 8080, or use 8092/`api-a` with `apiBaseUrlA`).

Run the items top to bottom. Steps 8-10 exercise the re-presentation: after the match is pending, kill the instance holding `tokenP1`, connect the same token to the other instance and send PING - the pending `MATCH_PENDING_CONFIRMATION` is sent again. The automated version is `requests/routing/verify_routing.sh`.

request.description: Player p1's socket lives on instance A. `redis-cli get presence:routing-a` now names api-a.
Player p2's socket lives on instance B: one match, two instances.
Expect PONG. While the match is pending, the same PING also re-presents `MATCH_PENDING_CONFIRMATION` (the client deduplicates by matchId).

item.name: 9. WS Connect p1 — instance B (A was killed)

request.description: Kill instance A (`kill -9 <pid>`) and reconnect the same token here: the player lands on instance B and the socket has not been pinned to anything.

item.name: 10. WS Send PING p1 on B — re-presents the pending match

request.description: Expect PONG and `MATCH_PENDING_CONFIRMATION` with the pending matchId - the notification A never delivered.
Any instance can finish the match: both confirmations go through B.

item.name: partitioning-w20 (queue partitions)
item.description: W20/ADR 0028: the queue is spread over QUEUE_PARTITIONS keys, hashed by the enqueue key (partyId or playerId). The full proof is `bash requests/partitioning/verify_partitioning.sh` (27 checks): start the API with QUEUE_PARTITIONS=8 on 8094 and the engine with QUEUE_PARTITIONS=8 on 9194, then run these requests and read the per-partition gauges. With QUEUE_PARTITIONS=1 (default) the key is the historical `queue:{mode}:{region}`.

item.name: GET /config
item.description:
Global compatibility level enforced by the Schema Registry (W12).

**Expected:** 200 with `{ "compatibilityLevel": "FULL" }`.

Set by `SCHEMA_REGISTRY_SCHEMA_COMPATIBILITY_LEVEL=full` in `docker-compose.yml`. It is the server-side half of the CI gate (W12 task 3): a new version of a subject must be readable by old AND new consumers, otherwise the registry rejects the registration.

Requires: `docker compose up -d zookeeper kafka schema-registry`.

item.name: GET /subjects

exec: pm.test('payload is a list of subjects', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.be.an('array'));

item.description:
Subjects registered in the `_schemas` topic.

**Expected:** 200 with `[]` until W12 task 2 registers the first event contract (`match-confirmed-value`, `player-search-value`).

A non-empty list here is also the proof that the registry reached the broker over the INTERNAL listener.

item.name: GET /schemas/types
item.description:
Schema formats this registry accepts.

**Expected:** 200 with `["JSON", "PROTOBUF", "AVRO"]`. The event contracts use Protobuf (see `04 - Engenharia Distribuída`).
